_comment: Guided tour for the PCH tool. Steps point at real controls; steps with an await wait for the user. The names file_loaded, computed and fitted are set by the app when the outcome exists, not when a button is pressed.

steps.title: What this measures
steps.text: The photon counting histogram P(k) says how often a time bin holds k photons. Its width beyond Poisson gives the molecular brightness and the number of molecules. Six steps: load, set up, compute, choose a range, fit, save.

steps.title: Load a photon stream
steps.text: Press Load TTTR and choose a PTU, HT3, T2R, T3R, PTO or SPC file, or drop it on the window.

await.hint: Press Load TTTR and choose a file to continue.

steps.title: Say which detectors count
steps.text: Channels lists the routing channels that are counted. The default 0,2 is only a starting point; use the channels of your detectors.

steps.title: Choose the counting interval
steps.text: Bin time is the width of one counting interval. Shorter than the diffusion time, so a molecule does not move much within a bin.

steps.title: Compute the histogram
steps.text: Compute PCH bins the photons and draws the intensity trace and the histogram P(k) on a logarithmic axis.

await.hint: Press Compute PCH and wait for the plots.

steps.title: Choose the k range of the fit
steps.text: Drag the two vertical lines on the histogram to set the lowest and highest k that the fit uses.

steps.title: Set the species
steps.text: Components is the number of species. Each row of the table is one species with a starting brightness ε and occupancy ⟨N⟩; double click a cell to change it.

steps.title: Fit the model
steps.text: Fit Model fits the species to the histogram over your k range. The table then shows the fitted ε and ⟨N⟩ and the results text the fractions and χ².

await.hint: Press Fit Model and read the fit results.

steps.title: Save the result
steps.text: Save Results writes the trace, histogram and fit as NPZ, CSV and TXT files under a base name you choose.
